title: When the Text Is Silent: Memory Shortcuts and the Validity of LLM Annotation under Evidence Insufficiency
summary: In controlled counterfactual texts about public figures and matched control names, three commercial LLMs produced labels unsupported by the text when evidence was absent. These memory shortcuts were often factually correct about a namesake but methodologically invalid as text-grounded annotations.
organization: Not stated in the abstract reviewed

evidence.tested: Across 995 public figures and four matched control names per figure, three commercial LLMs were evaluated on 121,594 prompts each. When text evidence was absent, one model increased remembered occupations, ages and countries by 17.0, 14.9 and 6.8 percentage points relative to synthetic names.
evidence.unknown: The results use selected models, entities and constructed prompts; they do not quantify all annotation settings.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
